newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling ends week firm.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling ends week firm.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling ended a week of sluggish trading on a touch firmer boosted by modest inflows from the agricultural sector, commercial bank dealers said.
The central bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 54.64 against the dollar from 54.65 while against the pound it was posted at 91.76 from 91.90.
Dealers said thin trading volumes and an absence of demand had sustained the shillings firm tone.
Some dealers said that they saw some demand for the shilling from foreign investors who were looking to buy treasury bills.
Another dealer said the central bank came in and bought the dollars at 54.68/69 which weakened the shilling temporarily at mid-morning.
"We do not think the shilling will weaken any further though, because the central bank took everything," he added.
Dealers said the shilling would continue to appreciate if current trends persisted.
The money market tightened with overnight rates quoted as high as 25 percent.
"Most banks are borrowing so they can build deposits and put them at above 18 percent so when the bad days come at least they can put them back to 18 percent," a dealer said.
Commercial banks are required to maintain an average of 18 percent of their total deposits with the central bank.
